newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq urges Iran to free all prisoners of war.
newsitem.headline: Iraq urges Iran to free all prisoners of war.

text.p: Iraq's National Assembly has called on Iran to free what it said were thousands of prisoners of war still held from the 1980-1988 Iraq-Iran war, state-owned newspapers said on Monday.

"The National Assembly called on Iran to free all Iraqi POWs and to cooperate with representatives of the International Committee of the Red Cross to establish the fate of those missing in action," the newspapers said.
Iran last month freed 150 Iraqi POWs and hundreds before that, but Baghdad wanted Iran to account for 20,000 other POWs. Iraq says it had freed all Iranian war prisoners.
Iraq and Iran signed an agreement last year on mutual relations and the issue of POWs, those missing in action (MIA) and remains of soldiers killed during the war.
Both countries have exchanged hundreds of POWs and remains of soldiers. In August the remains of 400 Iraqis and 65 Iranians were delivered to army officials of the two countries.

"Although 39,044 Iranian POWs have been returned to their country, there are still over 20,000 Iraqi POWs held in Iran. Red Cross representatives have not been permitted to visit them and Iranian authorities have not cooperated with regard to thousands of MIAs," the newspapers said.
They said Iraq was also preparing a working paper on Iraqi POWs.
